title: add jsonschema strict mode and OpenAI-compat response_format with improved error reporting
author: Sana Patel
description: Add JSONSchema strict response_format mode and OpenAI-compatible response_format semantics, and improve schema validation error messages. This change introduces a strict mode that enforces the assistant response to be a single top-level JSON value matching the provided JSON Schema. It also updates the OpenAI compatibility layer to accept response_format parameters (json_schema and strict=true/false) and returns structured error details for validation failures. Motivation: customer-reported regressions when using strict structured output combined with streaming and tool-calling; ambiguous validation errors made debugging prompts difficult. This PR: - adds a server-side strict validation path that runs once the response is complete (non-streaming) and as a best-effort checker for streaming responses, - improves error payload to include schema path, human-readable summary, and example remediation hint, - updates the OpenAI compatibility parser to map openai-style response_format arguments to Redwood's internal JSONSchema handling, - provides a configurable fallback policy to a non-strict validation result and explicit error codes when fallback is disabled, - adds unit and integration tests covering nested schemas, additionalProperties=false, required fields, and streaming fragments that close with trailing text, - updates docs and release notes and adds a migration note for existing customers who may rely on permissive outputs, - includes runtime telemetry hooks to surface validation failure rates and per-schema latency. The description below lists commits, changed areas, CI results, and review comments. NOTE: The PR intentionally keeps the runtime validation path opt-in (enabled when response_format=json_schema and strict=true) to avoid breaking customers who rely on permissive outputs.
commits: feat(response_format): implement jsonschema strict validation entrypoint
fix(openai-compat): map response_format params and normalize strict flag
test: add unit+integration tests for strict mode and streaming edge cases
docs: document strict mode behavior, fallback policies, and migration notes
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Please add a short-circuit early exit for streaming when strict=true to avoid buffering entire responses in memory. I think stream_validator can dispatch to heuristics to minimize memory pressure. Author: added stream-based heuristic that validates final complete output and keeps a running KV for bracket matching to detect early JSON completion; moved heavy validation off the streaming hot path.

Priya Rao: Error payload looks great but can we include schema pointer (JSON Pointer) and an example expected snippet? Author: included schema pointer and added a 'remediation_hint' field with a small JSON example when possible; also added API docs showing JSON schema error format.

Lukas Meyer: Integration tests failed on first run due to missing migration for existing saved prompts; suggest adding migration script or warning in logs. Author: added scripts/migrate_response_formats.py and logging to warn on deprecated stored response_format values.
Ethan Cole: nit: add more comments on strict_validator edge cases. Author: expanded inline comments and added unit tests covering edge cases.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (initial failure on migration, rerun fixed)
release_notes:
- Added JSONSchema strict response_format mode (response_format=json_schema, strict=true) that enforces a single top-level JSON value and validates against supplied schema.
- Improved schema validation error payloads: includes schema pointer, human summary, and remediation hints.
- OpenAI compatibility layer now supports response_format parameters and maps strict semantics.
- Added migration script and docs for customers using legacy/permissive response formats.
notes: Behavior is opt-in when strict=true. Streaming responses are best-effort validated; full enforcement requires non-streaming mode or post-hoc check. Customers should test pipelines when enabling strict mode; migration script will warn about saved prompts with deprecated flags.
